security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel code running at S-mode (not HS-mode or M-mode) accesses a CSR with csr[9:8]=10 (hypervisor-level CSR address range), triggering an illegal-instruction or virtual-instruction exception per the Zicsr privilege encoding convention now explicitly clarified to reserve pattern '10' for hypervisor CSRs.
security_spec.summary: Hypervisor CSR address range (csr[9:8]=10) is now normatively reserved for HS-mode access; kernel S-mode paths touching these CSRs directly will unconditionally fault, requiring audit of all RISC-V CSR access wrappers to ensure hypervisor CSRs are gated behind is_hs_mode() or kvm_arch entry guards.

findings.finding: Writes to hypervisor CSRs (CSR_HEDELEG=0x602, CSR_HIDELEG=0x603, CSR_HCOUNTEREN=0x606, CSR_HVIP=0x645, CSR_VSIE=0x204) are legitimate because KVM runs in HS-mode. The H-extension is verified present at module init (main.c:88). All accessed CSRs have csr[9:8]=10 which is the correct hypervisor encoding.

spec_citations.excerpt: The next two bits (csr[9:8]) encode the lowest privilege level that can access the CSR, with the pattern '10' representing hypervisor CSRs. [...] Attempts to access a CSR without appropriate privilege level raise illegal-instruction exceptions.

findings.finding: VCPU load path writes VS-level CSRs (CSR_VSSTATUS=0x200, CSR_VSIE=0x204, CSR_VSTVEC=0x205, etc.) and hypervisor CSRs (CSR_HEDELEG=0x602, CSR_HVIP=0x645, CSR_HENVCFG=0x60a). All accessed CSRs have csr[9:8]=10 (hypervisor range), which is valid for HS-mode execution after H-extension verification.

spec_citations.excerpt: The next two bits (csr[9:8]) encode the lowest privilege level that can access the CSR, with the pattern '10' representing hypervisor CSRs.

findings.finding: Suspend save/restore accesses only supervisor-level CSRs: CSR_ENVCFG=0x10a (csr[9:8]=01), CSR_STVEC=0x105 (csr[9:8]=01), CSR_SIE=0x104 (csr[9:8]=01), CSR_STIMECMP=0x14D (csr[9:8]=01), CSR_SATP=0x180 (csr[9:8]=01), CSR_SCRATCH=0x140 (csr[9:8]=01). No hypervisor CSR accesses.

Accesses M-mode CSRs (CSR_MVENDORID=0xf11, CSR_MARCHID=0xf12, CSR_MIMPID=0xf13, csr[9:8]=11) only under CONFIG_RISCV_M_MODE guard (line 205-210). Under S-mode, uses SBI calls instead (lines 199-204). No hypervisor CSRs are accessed in S-mode paths.
Accesses only CSR_STATUS (maps to CSR_SSTATUS=0x100 in S-mode, csr[9:8]=01) and CSR_ENVCFG=0x10a (csr[9:8]=01). Both are supervisor-level CSRs, correct for S-mode execution.
Accesses CSR_TH_SXSTATUS=0x5c0. csr[11:8]=0101, so csr[9:8]=01 (supervisor-level). Correctly in the custom S-mode read/write range (0x5C0-0x5FF per the CSR address table).

Checks CSR ranges CSR_VSTART=0x008 through CSR_VCSR=0x00F and CSR_VL=0xC20 through CSR_VLENB=0xC22. All are unprivileged CSRs (csr[9:8]=00 for VSTART-VCSR, csr[11:8]=1100 for VL-VLENB). Correct access level for any privilege mode.
Context switch writes CSR_ENVCFG=0x10a (csr[9:8]=01, supervisor-level). Correct for S-mode context switching. No hypervisor CSRs touched in the switch_to() fast path.
